items.author: Ben
items.title: Construction draws materials - in the opening years, and as centres grow
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-26: 'we need those first 20 years of generation to include construction'. MEASURED CONTEXT: materials are authored per building (resource_costs) and charged at the build press, but generation PLACES buildings rather than constructing them, so the draw never fires during the opening years - stone and timber have a construction sink on paper and no pull in practice. TWO HALVES, and the second is the one that lasts: (1) make the opening years actually build, so the warm start carries a real material pull; (2) make POPULATION CENTRES draw construction materials as they grow, which does not decay once the warm start ends. An ancient economy's largest material sink is building, and half (2) makes that structurally true rather than transiently.

RE-MEASURED 2026-09-01, and half (1)'s premise has moved (NR-773 carries the fork). ERAS.md settles what 'the first 20 years' means: they ARE app::start_new_game's 80-tick warm start, not a separate generation pass - and the warm start now constructs. Ancient-band construction-channel demand, blind census -> surveyed (NR-772) -> surveyed with BL-711: 93.25 -> 202.58 -> 210.08; timber's construct draw 54.0 -> 118.3, clay 0.0 -> 13.3. Much of what half (1) reached for arrived through BL-711 (the AI could previously only ever build iron_ore mines) and NR-772 (demand_census surveyed nothing, so it measured a world where the AI built no mines at all).

WHAT REMAINS TRUE OF HALF (1) is narrower: the SEEDER's ~330 buildings are authored complete - `author_building` writes a default ticks_remaining of 0 (corporation_generation.cpp) - and draw nothing, ever. Fixing that literally opens the campaign with 330 half-built buildings, which is a gameplay change rather than plumbing, so it wants Ben's reading.

HALF (2) is unambiguous in intent and has a clean hook already in place: economy_system.cpp's BL-616 growth block, where pcc.population takes a step and ++pcc.scale promotes. The one open question is whether the draw GATES growth or only registers a want - NR-773 options A/B/C, recommendation C (want now, gating its own item), because BL-641's cliff is the standing warning: a brand-new universal draw unmet on tick 1 collapsed operating firms 198/328 -> 33/317, and gating growth on an unmet draw is that same cliff pointed at population instead of firms.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Roads, ports and hubs draw materials to stay standing
items.design: The infrastructure demand channel (MARKETS.md section Demand channels). The logistics_maintenance budget line already exists and names exactly this, so the state half has a home. THE WORK: a network that consumes stone and timber to stay standing - a permanent sink scaled by GEOGRAPHY rather than by population, which is a shape none of the other channels has. Second-order and wanted: it gives reach a running cost, so extending the network becomes a decision rather than a ratchet. OWED: this item writes its paragraph into LOGISTICS.md; the design register in MARKETS.md points at it.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Government satellite launches - the tenth budget line, and space goods' first real buyer
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'add endpoints for space goods in government issued satellite launches'. Design in NATIONS.md section A budget. THE MACHINERY EXISTS - nations hold a weighted budget over priority lines, run_national_budget has claim/transfer machinery, and strategic_reserve is already a goods-buying line that no consumer claims on. THE WORK: a tenth line, space_programme, buying spacecraft_components and propellant through the BL-350 procurement seam (never on the open market - that is strategic_reserve's own rule). APPEND-ONLY: the weight vector is indexed by the enum and serialised, so the line goes last. Why it is worth more than a sink: state demand arrives in LUMPS and follows a weight a rival can lobby to move, so it is worth playing politics over rather than merely scaling into. ALSO OWNS spacecraft_components (BL-648's measurement, 2026-08-26): the guard's red list came back with ELEVEN goods, not the ten expected, and the eleventh is this one. Its exemption claimed BL-350 procurement, but procurement is a resource-agnostic TRANSFER between two corps' pools - it moves goods without consuming them, and admitting it as an injector would substantiate the entire roster at once. src/world contains no militia, and corp_ai.cpp says outright that the scorer does not emit those verbs today, so nothing automatic buys it. This line is its first real buyer.

items.title: Research consumes goods, not only credits
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'perhaps we could make research consume alternate goods as well'. Design written into RESEARCH.md. It gives the TOP of the production chain a buyer and turns the tech ladder into an economic decision rather than a free accumulator only time gates. Two properties: the basket is era-banded like every other, and a shortfall SLOWS research rather than voiding it (the same shape every goods draw takes). BLOCKED BY DESIGN on BL-619 (research system), which is a session with Ben - the rates, and whether the draw sits on the university or on the nation's budget lines, belong to that session rather than being settled ahead of it.

items.author: Ben
items.title: A battle consumes what it fires - conflict as a demand shock
items.design: The conflict demand channel (MARKETS.md section Demand channels). MEASURED: ordnance is priced at 43.00, near the top of the ancient roster, and its only draw is a per-head upkeep rate that BL-635's rescale took to 0.0035 - effectively nil. So the roster's most valuable military good has no buyer. THE WORK: a battle draws ordnance in proportion to what it commits, against the owner's pool, deterministically. WHY IT IS THE MOST INTERESTING OF THE EIGHT: it is the only channel that couples the game's two pillars - it makes Conflict move Trade, so a war somewhere else is a price signal here. OWED: this item writes its paragraph into MILITARY.md.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Tobacco, spices, coffee and furs get the buyer they were authored for
items.design: MEASURED: four endemic goods are on the roster, extractable, priced - and wanted by nothing at all, in any band. They pass the orphan check by naming 'mercantile demand', which BL-648 shows does not exist. THE WORK: a household demand that scales with WEALTH rather than headcount, flavoured by NATIONAL CHARACTER so different nations crave different luxuries. That asymmetry is the design, not a detail: it makes the trade route directional by construction - extract where it grows, sell where the money is - which is the most Trade-shaped channel of the eight and the one that most directly serves the pillar. Note it is also the first demand whose SIZE is a function of prosperity, so it rewards a player who has made somewhere rich.

items.title: The AI skill harness bands the spread in composite standing across the field, not absolute net worth
items.author: Ben
items.design:
AI_OPPONENT.md § The goal now makes a CLOSE RACE the intended shape of a campaign, produced by the world's brakes rather than by any agent's restraint. The instrument that scores the AI cannot see that quantity at all.

WHAT THE HARNESS MEASURES TODAY. Four per-seed metrics against golden bands: the net-worth curve (summed non-player balances), solvency ticks, survival fraction, and per-verb action counts. All four are absolute or aggregate. None can tell a run where every corp grew together from a run where one corp ran away - both sit inside a generous summed-net-worth band, and only the second is now a failure.

THE METRIC TO ADD. The spread between the leading corporation and the field, sampled on the existing SAMPLE_EVERY cadence. Held narrow is the pass; a widening gap is the regression. Exact form is the design call - leader-over-median and leader-over-second are both defensible, and the choice should be made against a real run's numbers rather than picked first (Rule 0b: report the observed spread with units, then choose).

THE ABSOLUTE BANDS DO NOT GO. They demote to a SOLVENCY FLOOR underneath the margin band. A world where the margin is beautifully narrow because every corp is broke is not a pass, and only the absolute figures can catch that.

CARRIED DEBT, and it belongs to whoever takes this item (NR-305): the current bands were blessed 2026-08-16 and are stale against everything since - possibly the mercenary contracts, the nation grants, or the roster widening. Re-derive from a fresh bless with dated provenance in the harness's own provenance-log idiom. Goldens here are disposable by project convention; the provenance comment is not.

ORDERING: this lands BEFORE BL-698 (scorer margin term). Building the objective before the measurement means tuning blind.

RETARGETED 2026-08-31 by Ben's systemic ruling. Two changes from the item as first minted:
  1. The banded quantity is the spread in COMPOSITE STANDING (BL-700, composite standing index), not in cash. Balance alone misreads the game constantly - a corp that just spent its treasury on a smelter is not behind.
  2. It is measuring whether THE WORLD'S BRAKES WORK, not whether an agent obeyed an instruction. No actor aims at the margin, so a widening spread is a finding about coalitions and climate, not about the scorer.

BEN'S FIRST-CUT TARGET, 2026-08-31: a leader roughly 28% ahead of the field. Treat that as the band to aim the SYSTEM at, not as a parameter to set anywhere - nothing in the code should know the number.

CARRIED OUT OF SPRINT 26, 2026-08-31, unbuilt and unscheduled. Ben closed that sprint at wave 1 once its own measurement showed every AI corp insolvent 29-30 ticks of 30 on every seed, with iron_ore produced 42991.6 against demand 0.000 on the industrial band (NR-758). This item's work is not wrong, it is UNMEASURABLE until demand exists: a coalition brake forms against 'whoever leads', and among corps that are all deeply insolvent the leader is merely the least bankrupt. Its tunables are the whole design and would need re-deriving against a solvent economy. Blocked on sprint 27's demand work rather than on any symbol - BL-642 names the first of it.

items.title: An opt-in margin dial scales a leading corp's whole candidate set - the difficulty knob, not the foundation
items.author: Ben
items.design:
DEMOTED 2026-08-31, the same day it was minted, by Ben's systemic ruling (AI_OPPONENT.md § Where restraint comes from). It was the sprint's centrepiece for about an hour. Read that section before this item - the demotion IS the design.

BEN'S OBJECTION, and it is correct: "The angle we are taking here is a literal handicap. I prefer to consider it as always a force from within the game system." A term in the scorer that says 'ease off, I am ahead' is invisible, uncausable and uncounterable. The player cannot see it, provoke it, benefit from it or fight it. It also buys its slim margin by making the AI worse, which § The goal forbids.

SO THIS IS NO LONGER HOW RESTRAINT HAPPENS. Coalitions (BL-699, rival coalitions) and climate (BL-701, living climate) are the foundation. This item survives ONLY as the explicit, opt-in DIFFICULTY KNOB Ben kept - "we can keep both modes" - and it is named as one, in the § 1 Area 4 sense of a small transparent economic handicap.

TWO HARD CONSTRAINTS, both from Ben, 2026-08-31.
  1. EVEN SCALING ACROSS EVERY CANDIDATE. Not a carve-out that discounts expansion and spares efficiency. Ben chose the even form deliberately over the surgical one.
  2. IT MAY NEVER VETO CONSTRUCTION OR EXTENSION. "'how far restraint goes' should never exclude extension and construction. If a player loses out, they should be able to see that the world doesn't wait for them." A dialled-down corp still builds, just less. A brake that freezes a leader destroys the honest consequence of falling behind, which is the thing the whole design protects.

OFF BY DEFAULT. The systemic route must be able to produce a close race on its own; if this dial is needed to get one, the brakes are the thing to fix. Ships as a mode, not as a default, and the harness bands the DEFAULT world.

Measured today for the record: corp_ai.cpp scores purely absolutely, and the only mention of `world::player_entity` is to EXCLUDE the player's corp (corp_ai.cpp:566-574, 625). Tunables live in corp_ai_params, per that file's own convention.

CARRIED OUT OF SPRINT 26, 2026-08-31, unbuilt and unscheduled. Ben closed that sprint at wave 1 once its own measurement showed every AI corp insolvent 29-30 ticks of 30 on every seed, with iron_ore produced 42991.6 against demand 0.000 on the industrial band (NR-758). This item's work is not wrong, it is UNMEASURABLE until demand exists: a coalition brake forms against 'whoever leads', and among corps that are all deeply insolvent the leader is merely the least bankrupt. Its tunables are the whole design and would need re-deriving against a solvent economy. Blocked on sprint 27's demand work rather than on any symbol - BL-642 names the first of it.

items.title: Rivals score stance against composite standing, so coalitions form against whoever leads
items.author: Ben
items.design:
PROMOTED 2026-08-31 from a nice-to-have to THE PRIMARY BRAKE. Ben: "With 7 corporations, we have plenty of room for alliances to form against leaders... I prefer if an agent's decision to slow down can be framed as usually motivated by systems." AI_OPPONENT.md § Where restraint comes from is the authority.

THE SHAPE. A rival's stance scoring reads WHO IS WINNING - the composite standing index from BL-700 (composite standing index). A corp near the top of the field attracts hostility; corps below it find each other worth befriending. The brake is applied TO the leader BY others, and no corp ever throttles itself. Every corporation keeps playing flat out; leading simply becomes expensive.

WHY THIS IS BETTER THAN A SCORER TERM, and why it is worth the extra difficulty: a coalition has a CAUSE, it is VISIBLE, and the player can join it, split it, provoke it or be its target. It converts the brake into gameplay. It also satisfies the standing rule that every system justify itself by feeding Trade or Conflict - a margin term feeds neither; a coalition feeds both.

THE VERBS ALREADY EXIST AND ARE UNUSED. corp_command.hpp carries four stance verbs from BL-448 - declare_hostile, offer_friendship, accept_friendship, return_to_neutral - specified, validated and serialised. corp_ai.cpp names NONE of them, so every rival is permanently neutral by omission rather than by choice. This item is the scoring that issues them; no new verb is needed.

THE PERMISSION EXISTS AND IS DATED. io-standing-rules.md carries Ben's 2026-08-22 grant for a rival scoring stance toward the player's corp, on the BL-450 terms - deterministic, seeded, scored-utility, legal verbs only, never a planner - and records that hostility stays a DECLARED state a corp opts into, never acquired ambiently. NOTE the provenance: BL-450 was PURGED in the 2026-08-23 cull, not completed; its prose is REFERENCE ONLY and this is authored fresh, per the cull's own resurrection rule.

THE COALITION MUST BE LEGIBLE OR IT IS JUST A HIDDEN HANDICAP AGAIN. That is the whole point of the reframe, so it is a requirement of this item and not a follow-up: a stance change emits into the § 7 chat channel and the decision feed, with its reason. A player must be able to SEE that the field has turned on the leader - and, when the leader is them, see it coming.

MUST NOT VETO EXTENSION (Ben, 2026-08-31). Coalition pressure makes leading costly; it never stops a corp building. See § The constraint on restraint.

OUT OF SCOPE: lobbying (nation-grain, purged as BL-539, unowned - NR-744), nation stance gating the player (BL-540, likewise), and the Stage C dialogue layer (BL-334, likewise).

CARRIED OUT OF SPRINT 26, 2026-08-31, unbuilt and unscheduled. Ben closed that sprint at wave 1 once its own measurement showed every AI corp insolvent 29-30 ticks of 30 on every seed, with iron_ore produced 42991.6 against demand 0.000 on the industrial band (NR-758). This item's work is not wrong, it is UNMEASURABLE until demand exists: a coalition brake forms against 'whoever leads', and among corps that are all deeply insolvent the leader is merely the least bankrupt. Its tunables are the whole design and would need re-deriving against a solvent economy. Blocked on sprint 27's demand work rather than on any symbol - BL-642 names the first of it.

items.title: Construction becomes a sector with a throughput and a production method, not a per-building lump sum
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-31: "we should parameterize construction. We can use construction as a rate, and pay upkeep on construction buildings which costs (depending on production method). The costs can be wood, iron, steel, e.t.c. Very similar to Victoria 3 in my mind." PRODUCTION.md § Construction as a rate is the authority.

THE CHANNEL IT FIXES. Construction demand measures 0.000 in the industrial band because run_construction fires only where something is actively building - it is episodic, and when nothing is under construction the channel is silent. A sector makes it CONTINUOUS and ECONOMY-SCALED: capacity exists, draws its method's goods as upkeep every tick, and grows with the world. MARKETS.md property 1 satisfied by construction rather than asserted of it.

BEN'S OWN REASON IS THE STRONGEST PART: "This makes it easy to start with some construction of a certain method, and gives us an initial demand for those construction goods." Seeded capacity gives non-zero demand from TICK 0 in every market that has any - which is MARKETS.md property 5's 'every chain terminates in every market' delivered by the generator rather than by authoring a basket. It is also an asymmetry lever: a region seeded on timber frame wants different goods, and is differently capable, from one seeded on steel.

FIVE METHODS, era-banded exactly as recipes are: timber frame and stone-and-brick (ancient); iron frame, steel frame and reinforced concrete (industrial). Baskets and rates are MEASURED against the census, never guessed. The ladder spans both bands deliberately, so the ancient band gains continuous construction demand too - it currently measures 56.3, better than zero and still episodic.

IT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT ADDITIVE, and that is why it sits after BL-708 (power as a grid) rather than beside it. It reaches construct_building, placement rules, the build door, and the AI scorer's capex model.

NR-592 IS FIXED HERE, on Ben's call ("With the construction change - it must reason about a shared pool"). corp_ai.cpp never prices resource_build_cost when scoring a build; a candidate scores on cash alone and the seam refuses it at apply time. Under a lump-sum model that is a missed opportunity. Under a SHARED CAPACITY POOL it becomes a correctness problem, because capacity is CONTENDED: a scorer blind to it will propose builds the pool cannot serve, every evaluation, for as long as the pool is short - which is the same thrash shape BL-696 just measured in the recipe margin-chase.

MEASURE BETWEEN THE TWO ITEMS. Run demand_census after BL-708 and again after this, so what power did and what construction did can be told apart.
items.summary:
VERIFIED 2026-09-01 and DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN. The code merged on 2026-08-31 (faf36725 / 26bc4fdd) and builds green, and the linter's false-open warning was right to say so — but the warning's own text is the correct reading here: *a partial slice can land under an item that is legitimately still open*. Three of four requirement rows verify; R1, the row the item exists for, does not.

R2 COMPLETE — five methods, era-banded, all group "Construction": timber_frame and stone_and_brick (ancient), iron_frame, steel_frame and reinforced_concrete (industrial), recipes.lua 827/842/857/874/889.
R3 COMPLETE — demand_census: `construction_capacity` is in the TERMINAL SET of both bands and priced in 14 of 14 ancient markets and 9 of 9 industrial, 0 floored, `in band` in both. MARKETS.md property 5 delivered by the generator, which is Ben's own stated reason for the change.
R4 COMPLETE — NR-592 cleared: `build_material_cost` is in the capex of both build candidates (corp_ai.cpp:951, :1202), keyed by recipe per BL-590. NR-592 marked resolved.
R1 PENDING — 'continuous and economy-scaled' is not what the world does. demand_census, ancient band: `construction_capacity` PRODUCED 0.0 over an 80-tick warm start with two timber-frame yards standing and both their inputs available (timber 5359.1, planks 635.8) — the yards exist and make nothing. chain_conversion_probe, industrial band: both seeded yards are GONE by tick 80, by removal rather than by switching (BL-712 confined the recipe chase to its own group, so it is not that). The census's `construct` column is still driven by live projects — the episodic behaviour this row was written to replace.

NOT AN OVERSIGHT, and that is why this is a known-hard row rather than a defect: economy.lua records that the obvious shape — capacity as a per-standing-building upkeep draw — was tried and MEASURED to collapse operating firms 198/328 -> 33/317, a cliff rather than a curve, the BL-641 collapse arriving through the cold start. NR-770 carries the diagnosis and points at BL-642 (construction draws), which owns the other half of the same fact.

Green on the way through: construction_harness, construction_gate_harness, upkeep_harness, and save_roundtrip at v22 — this item's own save bump, which had no working harness at all until BL-710 landed the same day.

items.title: A harness builds the world the application builds - one shared setup helper, not fifty independent guesses
items.author: Claude (review-queue drain, Ben's instruction)
items.design:
BEN'S RULING 2026-09-01 (NR-762): take this AFTER sprint 27 closes, not before the remaining channels - one golden wave, after the work that would otherwise move them twice.

THE DEFECT, counted exactly rather than estimated. `make_hard_coded_world` builds a world; `app::start_new_game` then runs a TAIL of passes on it; and the boundary between them is defined by nothing except which passes somebody remembered. **48 of the 51** harnesses that build a world never call `init_survey_states`. **22 of those also run the economy tick**, so the corp AI is live in a world where no body is surveyed and no rival can site a mine anywhere: acquisition_viability, cadence_schedule, convoy_cargo_census, data_creep_harness, debt_decomposition, decision_trace_harness, haulage_measure, history_log_harness, interbody_pull_harness, material_floor, nation_wiring, player_seed_sweep, population_demand_harness, population_mvp, pregame_balance_harness, quarterly_return, spawn_solvency, spectator_determinism, tech_effect_union_harness, tick_profile, tier_margin, whole_firm_buyout. That list holds most of this project's economic instruments.

THE FAILURE MODE IS THE WORST AVAILABLE: a harness measuring the wrong world does not go red, it reports confidently, and its goldens then encode that world. Three instances are on record - the default-recipe pass (2026-08-17), init_survey_states in ai_skill_harness (2026-08-31), and demand_census (2026-09-01, NR-772), the last of which made sprint 27's own primary instrument blind to half its work.

THE SHAPE is the one `no_prehistory()` already establishes: a shared helper in `harness_params.hpp` that a harness calls instead of hand-rolling its world setup, so the app-start tail is declared once.

FOLD IN, because they are the same subject - the build wiring that makes harnesses unbuildable or wrongly built:
* NR-767 - `harness_params.hpp` pulls sol2, so the Lua-linked class is large and GROWING while the only record is a hand-written list of six. Confirmed in the class and unlisted: save_roundtrip, world_determinism, determinism_harness, recipe_switch_harness, build_spree_harness, decision_trace_harness, ai_skill_harness, spectator_determinism, upkeep_harness, chain_conversion_probe. DERIVE the routing (detect the transitive include and delegate, or fail with a one-line message naming the right builder) rather than listing it.
* NR-617 - `build_harness.js`'s LUA_TUS exclusion list is stale; contract_template.cpp needs sol2 and is not in it.
* NR-721 - ~30 harnesses could not compile from a clean configure since the v0.1.21 cut, and a release passed anyway.
* NR-755 - `build_app.bat` hard-fails in a fresh worktree because `build/` is gitignored and it does not cold-configure.
* NR-730 - no harness compiles `src/ui` or `src/core`, so a worktree agent cannot build what it changes.
* NR-759 - four build-wiring breaks in one session, none caught by any test, two MASKED BY STALE BINARIES THAT PASSED. A stale prebuilt exe reporting green on a world that no longer exists is the same class as this whole item.
* NR-771 - `ai_skill_harness`'s hand-built registry holds three recipes with no `group`, so it is structurally blind to any per-category change (BL-712 returned byte-identical numbers before and after). Either give it real groups or move it onto the Lua registry.

items.title: Four verification instruments pass without seeing their subject, and one hangs the suite
items.author: Claude (review-queue drain, Ben's instruction)
items.design:
A green check that cannot see its subject is worse than a red one, and five are on record. Grouped because the fix is one discipline - a check must prove it LOOKED - not five unrelated repairs.

* NR-614 / NR-663 - `expect_no_clipping`'s scope is draw-list text only, so it reported '0 failure(s), 0 record(s)' over a whole 31-capture shell pass while the Corporation dashboard visibly truncated 'Workforce 76% of labour demand n' mid-word and a genuinely clipped button was on screen. ZERO RECORDS is the tell: the ledger saw nothing, so the pass is vacuous. Any check that can report zero observations must FAIL on zero, not pass.
* NR-714 - `budget_ledger_ranked.lua` is named for the Balance ledger's top-buildings ranking and captures two frames, neither of which contains it (one scrolled past it, one with the ledger shut).
* NR-606 / NR-623 - four verify scripts fail for pre-sprint reasons and `lens_strip`'s three goldens are stale by world drift (blessed 2026-06-17). The strip is the subject; the map behind it is not - re-point them at something world-independent or retire them to capture-only.
* NR-695 - `overflow_tile_v2` hung the suite: the History ledger's TILES view is a row per tile on the body, so the sweep burned CPU, collapsed memory and starved nine scripts behind it. A per-script wall clock would have turned a suite-wide stall into one red row.

items.short_name: the save seam past the world
items.title: The envelope has no round-trip coverage, a loaded save does not render as the world it was saved from, and the comms log is dropped
items.author: Claude (review-queue drain, Ben's instruction)
items.design:
`save_roundtrip` covers `world`. Nothing covers the rest of the file, and three findings say so.

* NR-708 - NO ENVELOPE FIELD HAS ROUND-TRIP COVERAGE, and `save_game_version` has already moved (1 -> 2) with strict-equality refusal, so every existing save became unreadable on a change nothing verified. Flat binary serialisation is the project's chosen persistence (TECH_FOUNDATIONS.md refuses SQLite for it), which makes this exactly the gap BL-710 just closed on the other half of the file.
* NR-608 - a loaded save does not RENDER as the world it was saved from. Measured in both directions: `player_balance` returns bit-identical, but `world::state_hash` does not round-trip once any econ tick has run (7161C70488A767CA -> 62CAB4412DEDC7E0) while a zero-tick world does round-trip exactly - which localises it to the day-tick mirror being rewound rather than to the world store.
* NR-609 - the comms log is excluded from the envelope as 'transient view state'. It is not: it is the record of what happened in the campaign, and the dock comes back empty after any load.
* NR-768 - `save_roundtrip` verifies a `resource_count` bump only INCIDENTALLY; it never names the constant. Two of the last three save bumps were per-resource widenings, so that is now the format's most common change and the one it asserts least directly. One cheap row fixes it.

items.title: The tech tree is ~150 nodes of data nothing reads, and the gates that DO resolve point at the wrong nodes
items.author: Claude (review-queue drain, Ben's instruction)
items.design:
Four findings, one subject, and the third makes it player-visible rather than merely inert.

* NR-591 - `scripts/tech_tree.lua` opens with 'DATA ONLY - the tech system is post-prototype; nothing in the simulation reads this', and the simulation's gate table is authored independently of it.
* NR-728 - THE IDS DO NOT LINE UP, so the F9 viewer shows the wrong unlock: `E0-EC-01` is the simulation's Toolmaker unlock and tech_tree.lua line 408 calls that id 'Semiconductor Fabrication'. A viewer that confidently names the wrong technology is worse than one that names none.
* NR-594 - `tech_gate_harness` only exercises E0-ML-01; the three economy gates (E0-EC-01/02/03) are proven live only indirectly.
* NR-751 - the Era renumber left the viewer's tab labels reading the old numbers.

Sequencing note from NR-750: the Era catastrophe model was PROMOTED into ERAS.md from a research doc and its original owner (BL-087) was purged, so the era/tech/quest system currently has no owner at all. This item is the nearest thing; a real era owner should be minted when that work is next, per the cull's resurrection rule.

items.title: Two designed mechanisms compute their result and drop it on the floor - interception and the LP refusal
items.author: Claude (review-queue drain, Ben's instruction)
items.design:
LOGISTICS.md's own clause is the test both of these fail: *announced in the same change that resolves it - silence is the wrong default* (NR-407).

* NR-599 - every `interception_record` is computed and DISCARDED; the `out_cuts` sink has no production caller, so interdiction resolves invisibly. Interdiction's core landed 2026-08-21 and the narration was deleted with Sprint 25b.
* NR-624 - `run_unit_march` COUNTS the LP refusal and drops the count. LOGISTICS.md § Refusal, surface and determinism carries two duties; BL-606 discharged the lens half and left this one. 'A refusal nobody sees is silent interdiction again' is the doc's own sentence.

Both are wiring rather than design: carry the count into `economy_report` and surface it where the player already looks at movement. The decision feed is the natural home for both.

items.short_name: the name column is one character
items.title: Three surfaces truncate every name to a single character, and the mechanism is shared
items.author: Claude (review-queue drain, Ben's instruction)
items.design:
* NR-613 / NR-709 - nav slot 8's corporations table allots the NAME column roughly ten pixels, so every row reads as one letter (F, E, C, G, T, N, Y, Q, H, Z, B, S) and the header 'C' is itself the truncated word. The capture pass found the SAME defect on two more surfaces, so it is a class: the fold-out column host is ~358px and every stretch NAME column starves inside it. Fix the host, not the three tables.

FOLD IN, same surfaces, same pass, and player-visible:
* NR-612 / NR-713 - internal identifiers leak into player-facing UI: 'Policy levers - not yet wired (BL-155)' in the Budget ledger, 'BL-087 design mock - read-only.' in the Research panel, 'First cut (BL-660)' in Tectonics, 'Province #2' in Contracts, and 'Era 2 (unauthored)' offered to the player as a CHOICE. A player cannot resolve a BL- id, so the string says only that the game is unfinished.
* NR-704 - `show_corporation_panel` drives the dashboard and `show_corporations_table` drives the panel: each `ui_state` flag names the other one's function. Not tidiness - it is a trap for anyone wiring either surface.

items.short_name: shell defects from the capture pass
items.title: Seven shell and canvas defects found in the capture passes, none of them owned
items.author: Claude (review-queue drain, Ben's instruction)
items.design:
Filed together because none is big enough to carry an item and all of them are on surfaces a player touches.

* NR-597 - the corp-selection screen's per-row 'Choose' buttons DO NOT RESPOND TO CLICKS. Reproducible on corp_choice.lua's live surface; likely a handler wired to the row highlight and not the button. Ben ruled it not urgent at the time, but it is a dead control on the first screen of a new campaign.
* NR-601 - six of the seven gradient-bar lens keys are drawn UNDERNEATH the Selection band and cannot be read.
* NR-611 - the Selection band's resting state is ~90% empty and its action grid is six near-identical circles.
* NR-615 - the system menu offers only Resume and Exit Game. Quick save/load exist on F5/F6 and display options exist, and none of the three is reachable, so a player who does not know the keys cannot save or discover saving.
* NR-625 - two surfaces report different grid dimensions for the same body (Generation Ledger 180x84, canvas caption 261x121).
* NR-723 - the nav rail's fourteenth slot puts its centre at y=746 on a 720px display, so the Contracts ledger is DRAWN AND UNREACHABLE - visible, apparently fine, inert. Invisible at 1080p, which is why nothing caught it.
* NR-700 - a corporation-structure hit opens the PLAYER'S OWN balance ledger, so the Corporation lens's click destination is wrong under the one-tier rule.
* NR-626 - every decision in the AI feed reads 'overridden' with a chosen score of 0.00. Re-check against the current scorer before investigating: BL-417 changed the score's magnitude entirely, so the reading may have moved or resolved.

items.short_name: the seeder cannot see processing demand
items.title: The world seeder sizes against consumer demand only, so any chain whose raw no consumer wants is never mined
items.author: Claude (review-queue drain, Ben's instruction)
items.design:
NR-766, filed as novel-work by the BL-708 slice and never given an owner.

`body_demand` counts household baskets plus the background stopgap. It never counts what PROCESSORS need as inputs - which is the larger half, and the difference between a world seeded to feed its own chains and one seeded to feed its households and hope.

BL-708 patched the UPKEEP half (`body_upkeep_demand`, re-measured per iteration because placing a firm creates its own draw). The processing-input half is still unseen.

PART OF THE PREMISE HAS SINCE BEEN ANSWERED FROM THE OTHER END, and the item should be re-measured before it is built: NR-766's headline example was that coal is produced 0.0 because nothing consumes it directly, so the seeder never sized for it and no coal mine was ever placed. BL-711 (per-resource extraction ranking) now has the AI building 25 coal mines on the industrial band and 17 on the ancient one, and coal produced 0.0 -> 632.7. So the SCORER half of that deadlock is fixed; what remains is whether GENERATION should still seed against it, which is a smaller and cleaner question than the entry was written against.

It is generation-layer work made by an economy slice whose brief did not name it - generation-dev's eyes, not an economy agent's judgement call.

items.short_name: paid for outcomes has no mechanism
items.title: Retiring the mercenary contract left CONCEPT.md's core player identity with nothing behind it
items.author: Claude (review-queue drain, Ben's instruction)
items.design:
NR-729. Ben retired the mercenary contract on 2026-08-29 and two authority claims lost their mechanism. Both are load-bearing rather than decorative, which is why this is a design item rather than a doc tidy.

* CONCEPT.md § Player identity: *'The player is a mercenary company... it is armed and for hire... and it is PAID FOR OUTCOMES.'* Nothing now pays for an outcome. Procurement pays for GOODS DELIVERED, which is a different promise.
* SYSTEMS.md § The progression chain has a link with no mechanism where the contract sat.

EITHER re-point the identity at what the game actually rewards (delivery, standing, territory), OR mint the mechanism that pays for an outcome. The first is a doc change and an honest one; the second is a system. It is a CONCEPT-level call and it should not be settled by whoever next reads the paragraph.

Related and worth taking in the same pass: NR-744 - three purged AI items (BL-539 rival lobbying, BL-540 nation stance gates the player, BL-334 Stage C dialogue) still hold DATED STANDING-RULE GRANTS in io-standing-rules.md and have no owner, so the rules cite items that no longer exist.

items.title: Three UI requirements shipped render-confirmed only, because nothing in the container can approve the OS consent dialog
items.author: Claude (review-queue drain, Ben's instruction)
items.design:
The standing rule is that a UI requirement needs a LIVE CLICK, not a scripted capture (io-standing-rules.md; DELIVERY.md step 4). Three items could not have one and said so rather than quietly marking the requirement complete - NR-593 (BL-591's growth-track readout), NR-595 (BL-593's tech-lock filter, which additionally could not scroll the tile build ledger into view), NR-622 (BL-606's Throughput lens).

THE CAUSE IS ENVIRONMENTAL, NOT PROCEDURAL: `request_access` for ProjectIo returns `notInstalled` or `user_denied` because the app is a custom .exe outside the Windows Start-Menu registry, and nothing in the container can approve the consent dialog.

TWO THINGS THIS ITEM OWES. (1) A route that makes a live press possible from a session at all - a registered shortcut, a Start-Menu entry, or a documented manual step Ben performs. (2) A `scroll_panel` case for the tile build ledger, whose dynamic 'Construct [x, y]' title the existing helper cannot target. Until (1) exists the rule is unenforceable, and a rule nobody can satisfy gets quietly dropped - which is how the three above accumulated.
